transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I'm feeling incredibly anxious and I don't know where else to turn. I am absolutely certain that a specific organization is monitoring my every move and watching me constantly. I just need help dealing with the stress of being targeted like this.

Have you ever heard or seen things that other people couldn’t, or had these beliefs during a time when you were not severely depressed or unusually energetic with little need for sleep? Have these experiences happened only when your mood was very low or very high?
No, I don't hear or see things that aren't actually there. My mood has also been pretty stable without any extreme highs or lows, other than the constant anxiety from being watched.
Aside from this belief that you’re being watched, have you had major problems with work, daily self-care, or getting along with people? Or have you mostly been able to function normally?

I've mostly been able to function normally, keep my job, and take care of myself. The only real issue is the constant stress and the extra precautions I have to take daily to protect my privacy from them. Other than that, my routine is pretty standard.
How long have you been convinced that this organization is monitoring you? Has this belief been present for at least one month?

Yes, it has been going on for much longer than just a month. It started about seven months ago, and there hasn't been a single day since then where they haven't been watching me. I am absolutely certain of the timeline.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["Delusional Disorder"], and based on this conversation that remains the same. The patient describes a fixed persecutory belief lasting 7 months, denies hallucinations, denies episodes of mania or major depression tied to the belief, and reports largely preserved functioning aside from behavior related to the belief. This makes schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, bipolar disorder with psychotic features, and major depressive disorder with psychotic features less likely, so the candidate list remains ["Delusional Disorder"].
